english: The twin spoke to the man. "Seize me, brother, and cut me." "May my flesh become the earth." "May my bones become stones." "May my blood become the sea." "May my head become the sky." Then the gods set a famous name for the twin. He went away and looked at the stars.

english: The twin lay on the strewn place. The gods arrived, and they sat down around him. Then they slit him open. They cut the flesh from the bones. From it they made the earth, and they broke the bones. Then from them they made stones. The blood ran out. Then from it they made the waters. They cut off his head. Then from it they created the sky. From his mind the moon came forth. Then from his tears came the rain-clouds. Then it rained. They set the sun above, and they threw the stars into the night. Then they saw their work. And it was good. They walked on it. They drank the waters, and they became joyful.

english: The first man and the twin were brothers. Together they drove the sheep and the cattle into the field, and they found a strewn place under an oak. The oak was old. Then there the man built a hearth. He gave the fire libated honey. The gods spoke to him: "Make the sacrifice." "Seize your dear twin." He heard their word, and his heart trembled. Then he seized the twin and slew him. The twin did not cry out. That was the first sacrifice. He sat down by the hearth, and he did not speak. Then from the twin's flesh the earth came forth. From his head the sky was made. It was broad. Then from his blood the sea arose. And they gave the man good fame. He became the begetter of the people. Then the twin's name became famous.

"Give us water and wool." "Let them be many."

Then having stolen the fire in the gods' hearth, he carried it to the people. The night hid him. Then he ran to them. The thief was swift. The fire burned in their hearths, and they became warm. They became glad. They cooked and ate. The thief's name is famous.

Your fields are broad. Beasts and cattle drink your waters. Give us wool and honey! Mother, may you carry us and the beasts! When we die, cover our bones.

Sleep comes to us and to the beasts. You are the mother of the stars and of Dawn. Do not frighten our flock, Night! May Dawn, daughter of Sky, come to us!

english: Sky and Earth lay together. The sons dwelt in between. They trembled. Then they grew strong. Then the great son rose. He looked at them and spoke: "Let us lift Sky up." "Let us set her down." Standing, they lifted him up. And they set her down. Then it became bright. Then the mist went away. They caught sight of the sun and became joyful. He stood above, and she lay below. The sun goes in between.

Héh₂mr̥h₂ dl̥h₁gʰéh₂ bʰuHyéti. tépos h₂ékʷās h₂sowséyeti. sóh₂wl̥ kʷélh₁t ǵʰéymn̥-kʷe léytt. snóygʷʰōs tinéh₁ti h₂éndʰōs-kʷe h₂éǵroy bʰwéh₂t. h₂óweyes h₂uksént h₁éḱwōs-kʷe h₂uksént. kʷís h₁ludʰéyey ǵʰwērbʰós-kʷe ḱód h₂réydʰet? deywṓs h₁éymos ḱód h₂réydʰont.
english: Night comes, and day comes. The sun walks in the day. The stars stand in the sky. Winter comes, and the waters grow cold. The days grow long. Heat dries the waters. The sun turns, and winter goes. The snow melts, and blossoms arise in the field. The sheep grow, and the horses grow. Who set this in order for the people and the beasts? The gods set this in order for them.

HéHḱewes h₁éḱwōs kʷékʷlom dukénti. sh₂wéns kʷékʷlos HéHḱus h₁ésti. h₂éwsōs h₂wést nu sóh₂wl̥ léwkt. sóh₂wl̥ kʷsépi séngʷt Héh₂m̥ni-kʷe léwkt. sh₂wéns kʷékʷlos ne Hrumptór. h₁ésyo stóygʰos h₃reǵtós h₁ésti. sóh₂wl̥ h₂ékʷās gʷʰr̥néwti. sóh₂wl̥ nos ǵʰwḗrn̥s-kʷe dedórḱe. sóh₂wl̥ nos dedr̥ḱyéh₁t h₁íd nos ḱluyéh₁t.
english: The wheel of the sun runs through the sky. Swift horses draw it. Swift is the wheel of the sun. Dawn dawns, then the sun becomes bright. In the night the sun sinks, and in the day it becomes bright. The wheel of the sun does not break. Its path is straight. The sun heats the waters. The sun sees us and the beasts. May the sun see us, may it hear us.

english: May the cattle stand there, may they not flee! May the wolf not come to them! May the snake and the thief not seize them! Dog, guard the sheep and the flock! Shepherd, drive them inside! Sky, give water, Earth, nourish them! May they be many, may they grow! May the king have imperishable fame! May the king's flock be great and many!

english: Dawn, daughter of Sky, become bright! You who awaken the people and the beasts, you who drive the night away. You who bring the swift light of the sun. You clothe yourself in a broad garment. When you come, the night grows less. Your light is great. Come to our hearth, Dawn! Awaken us, Dawn, daughter of Sky!

english: Desire arose first, from Desire the mind arose. Who stretched the sky? Who laid the earth below? Who made the sea and the oak? Who set the sun and the moon above? Who yoked the swift horses to the wheel of the sun? Who gave the day and the light to the mortals? The gods know it, and we do not know it. Let us make a sacrifice to them.

english: A sheep that had no wool saw horses, one of them pulling a heavy wagon, one carrying a big load, and one carrying a man quickly.
